title: Prove each run repeats, and start from last cycle's plan

blocks.text: Problem statement
The planner is now used for the real portfolio, GridCap medium in this course: 400 projects over ten years (fictional, like all GridCap data). Audit and the planning lead sent the last requests:
Audit: if we run the same export twice we must get the same plan, and every run must say what it was planned from and with what. Prove it.

Planning lead: the rule tests are good, but last month a change to the window code moved projects and no test noticed. And each run takes half a minute now; next cycle starts from this cycle's plan, so can the solver start from it too?

You start from the planner with scenarios and snapshots. Identify a plan by a digest of its content, rerun an export from scratch and show whether the runs agree, and record for each run what it was planned from and with which solver and settings. Check today's plan of a fixed export against a reviewed golden plan and list every project whose start moved, including one the golden plan never funded. Let a solve start from last cycle's plan, keeping only the starts the new model still has, and give the same plan as a solve from nothing.

A plan's canonical JSON is that of the store: sorted keys, no spaces after `,` and `:`. A golden file is one JSON object with the keys `input` (the export's content hash), `npv`, `starts` and `status`, written with sorted keys, an indent of one space and a final newline. When the export's hash differs from the golden file's `input`, the check returns the single line `input changed: golden <first 12 hex digits>, now <first 12 hex digits>`. A hint reaches HiGHS as `mathopt.ModelSolveParameters(solution_hints=[mathopt.SolutionHint(variable_values=...)])`, passed to `mathopt.solve` as `model_params`, with the variables of this model as keys.

Run's report gains a line: `main.py` now plans the demo export three times and says whether the plans agree. After the scenario section it prints an empty line, then `3 runs, same plan: <True or False>, plan digest <12 hex digits>`, the digits being the start of the first run's plan digest. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Blueprint
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.
`plan_digest` in `cipt/trust.py`
def plan_digest(plan: Plan) -> str

items: **Contract.** Returns the sha256 hex digest of the plan's canonical JSON, status and starts only.
**Modeling idea.** Two runs agree exactly when their plan digests do.

**Taught in** [10.2.5 Building the Deterministic Run Harness](../../../../10-numerics-and-determinism/41-determinism-and-reproducibility/units/unit-05/10.2.5-building-the-deterministic-run-harness.unit.html).

**Taught in** [10.2.5 Building the Deterministic Run Harness](../../../../10-numerics-and-determinism/41-determinism-and-reproducibility/units/unit-05/10.2.5-building-the-deterministic-run-harness.unit.html).

def manifest(raw: dict, scenario: Scenario, plan: Plan) -> dict

items: **Contract.** Returns what a run depended on: the export's content hash as input, the scenario as a dictionary, the solver (name HIGHS, the OR-Tools version, the thread count), the plan's digest and its NPV rounded to cents.
**Modeling idea.** A run is reproducible when its manifest pins the input, the settings and the solver.

**Taught in** [10.2.4 Versioned Input Snapshots, Pinned Solvers and Run Manifests](../../../../10-numerics-and-determinism/41-determinism-and-reproducibility/units/unit-04/10.2.4-versioned-input-snapshots-pinned-solvers-and-run-manifests.unit.html).

blocks.text: `check_golden` in `cipt/trust.py`
def check_golden(raw: dict, path: str | Path) -> list[str]

items: **Contract.** Returns every way today's plan of the export differs from the golden file: a changed input alone when the hashes differ (`input changed: golden <12 hex digits>, now <12 hex digits>`); otherwise, in this order, `status <golden> -> <now>` when the status differs, each project whose start differs as `<id>: start <golden> -> <now>` over the projects of both plans in id order (`None` for a project a plan does not fund), and `npv <golden> -> <now>` (whole $k, thousands commas) when the NPV moves by more than 0.5. Empty when they agree.
**Modeling idea.** A golden test pins a reviewed plan of a fixed input, so a change that moves the plan fails until someone reviews it.

**Taught in** [12.3.3 Golden Datasets and Regression Tests](../../../../12-engineering-the-optimization-service/47-testing-optimization-code/units/unit-03/12.3.3-golden-datasets-and-regression-tests.unit.html).

"""python -m cipt EXPORT.json [--why PROJECT]: plan the export and print the report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from .data import read_request
from .diagnose import why_deferred, why_infeasible
from .report import render
from .solve import solve


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cipt", description="Plan a capital portfolio.")
    parser.add_argument("export", help="the planning export, a JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--why", metavar="PROJECT", help="explain why PROJECT was not funded")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    request = read_request(args.export)
    plan = solve(request)
    print(render(request, plan))
    if plan.status == "infeasible":
        print(why_infeasible(request).message)
        return 1
    if args.why and args.why not in plan.starts:
        d = why_deferred(request, plan, args.why)
        if d.conflict:
            print(f"{args.why} cannot be funded. {d.conflict.message}")
        else:
            print(f"Funding {args.why} costs ${d.npv_cost:,.0f}k of NPV and drops {', '.join(d.displaced) or 'nothing'}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Two goals at once: the trade between NPV and the risk a plan removes.

`frontier` finds plans none of which beats another on both goals, by the epsilon-constraint
method (lesson 8.3.1): maximize NPV while the risk removed must reach a floor, for floors spread
between the two single-goal plans. Each point is finished by a second, lexicographic solve
(lesson 8.2.1) that keeps its NPV and takes as much risk as that NPV allows, so no point is beaten
on one goal by a plan equal on the other (lesson 8.3.2).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from .data import Request
from .model import build
from .plan import Plan
from .solve import solve_built

#: Slack on a goal a second pass must keep: NPV is whole $k; risk is a float sum.
KEEP = {"npv": 0.5, "risk": 1e-6}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Point:
    npv: float
    risk: float
    plan: Plan


def best(request: Request, first: str, floor: float | None = None) -> Plan:
    """Maximize `first`, then the other goal with `first` held at its best (two solves)."""
    built = build(request)
    goal = {"npv": built.npv, "risk": built.risk}
    if floor is not None:
        built.add("risk_floor", built.risk >= floor)
    built.model.maximize(goal[first])
    plan = solve_built(built)
    if plan.status != "optimal":
        return plan
    other = "risk" if first == "npv" else "npv"
    built.add(f"keep_{first}", goal[first] >= getattr(plan, first) - KEEP[first])
    built.model.maximize(goal[other])
    return solve_built(built)


def dominates(a: Point, b: Point) -> bool:
    return a.npv >= b.npv - KEEP["npv"] and a.risk >= b.risk - KEEP["risk"] and \
        (a.npv > b.npv + KEEP["npv"] or a.risk > b.risk + KEEP["risk"])


def frontier(request: Request, points: int = 5) -> list[Point]:
    """Up to `points` non-dominated plans, from the best NPV to the most risk removed."""
    ends = [best(request, "npv"), best(request, "risk")]
    if any(p.status != "optimal" for p in ends):
        return []
    low, high = ends[0].risk, ends[1].risk
    plans = [ends[0]]
    for k in range(1, points - 1):
        plans.append(best(request, "npv", floor=low + k * (high - low) / (points - 1)))
    plans.append(ends[1])
    found: list[Point] = []
    for plan in plans:
        point = Point(plan.npv, plan.risk, plan)
        if plan.status == "optimal" and not any(abs(point.npv - q.npv) <= KEEP["npv"] for q in found):
            found.append(point)
    return [p for p in found if not any(dominates(q, p) for q in found)]

"""A plan: what the solve decided, in the planners' terms."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    """The answer to a request.

    `status` is "optimal", "infeasible" or another solver outcome in lower case; `starts` maps each
    funded project to the year its work starts; `objective` is what the model maximized; `npv` and
    `risk` are the plan's NPV and the risk it removes, both in $k, whichever was maximized.
    """

    status: str
    starts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    objective: float = 0.0
    npv: float = 0.0
    risk: float = 0.0

    @property
    def funded(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(sorted(self.starts))

"""Solve a request with HiGHS and read the answer back as a Plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import sys

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt
from ortools.math_opt.solvers import highs_pb2

from .data import Request
from .model import Built, build
from .plan import Plan

#: One thread, set in HiGHS's own options; the first HiGHS solve of a process fixes the count.
PARAMS = mathopt.SolveParameters(highs=highs_pb2.HighsOptionsProto(int_options={"threads": 1}))


def run_highs(model: mathopt.Model, hint: dict | None = None) -> mathopt.SolveResult:
    """Solve with stdout pointed at /dev/null, so HiGHS's stray C output stays out of reports.

    `hint` maps variables to values: a starting plan HiGHS may use (lesson 11.2.1).
    """
    model_params = mathopt.ModelSolveParameters(solution_hints=[mathopt.SolutionHint(variable_values=hint)]) \
        if hint else None
    sys.stdout.flush()
    saved, sink = os.dup(1), os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    os.dup2(sink, 1)
    try:
        return mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=PARAMS, model_params=model_params)
    finally:
        ctypes.CDLL(None).fflush(None)
        os.dup2(saved, 1)
        os.close(saved)
        os.close(sink)


def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan:
    """Turn a solver result into a Plan: each funded project with the year its x is 1."""
    status = result.termination.reason.name.lower()
    if not result.has_primal_feasible_solution():
        return Plan(status=status)
    values = result.variable_values()
    starts = {pid: t for (pid, t), var in built.x.items() if values[var] > 0.5}
    return Plan(status=status, starts=starts, objective=result.objective_value(),
                npv=mathopt.evaluate_expression(built.npv, values),
                risk=mathopt.evaluate_expression(built.risk, values))


def solve(request: Request, previous: Plan | None = None) -> Plan:
    """Plan a request; `previous`, last cycle's plan, is handed to HiGHS as a start when given."""
    built = build(request)
    hint = None if previous is None else {built.x[key]: v for key, v in hint_values(built, previous).items()}
    return read_plan(built, run_highs(built.model, hint))


def hint_values(built: Built, previous: Plan) -> dict[tuple[str, int], float]:
    """Last plan's starts on this model's variables: 1 where it still has the variable, else 0.

    A start the window no longer allows, or a project that left the export, is dropped, so the
    hint never names a variable that does not exist.
    """
    return {key: float(previous.starts.get(key[0]) == key[1]) for key in built.x}


def solve_built(built: Built) -> Plan:
    """Solve a model the caller may have changed (a new objective, an extra row) after `build`."""
    return read_plan(built, run_highs(built.model))
File: cipt/store.py

"""Snapshots, scenarios and runs in one SQLite file (lesson 12.1.4).

A snapshot is the export exactly as received, stored as canonical JSON under the sha256 of that
JSON, so a run can always be traced to the bytes it planned from, and a changed byte is caught when
the snapshot is read. A run stores the scenario, the snapshot's hash and the plan it produced.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from .data import load_request
from .plan import Plan
from .scenario import Scenario, apply
from .solve import solve

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshot (hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scenario (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, snapshot TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES snapshot(hash),
                                     body TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, scenario TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES scenario(name),
                                snapshot TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, npv REAL, risk REAL,
                                starts TEXT NOT NULL);
"""


def canonical(raw: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(raw, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def content_hash(raw: dict) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(raw).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class Store:
    def __init__(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)

    def save_snapshot(self, raw: dict) -> str:
        digest = content_hash(raw)
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO snapshot VALUES (?, ?)", (digest, canonical(raw)))
        return digest

    def snapshot(self, digest: str) -> dict:
        (body,) = self.db.execute("SELECT body FROM snapshot WHERE hash = ?", (digest,)).fetchone()
        raw = json.loads(body)
        if content_hash(raw) != digest:
            raise ValueError(f"snapshot {digest[:12]} does not match its hash")
        return raw

    def save_scenario(self, scenario: Scenario, snapshot: str) -> None:
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO scenario VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                            (scenario.name, snapshot, canonical(scenario.to_dict())))

    def scenario(self, name: str) -> tuple[Scenario, str]:
        body, snapshot = self.db.execute("SELECT body, snapshot FROM scenario WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchone()
        return Scenario.from_dict(json.loads(body)), snapshot

    def run(self, name: str) -> Plan:
        """Plan a stored scenario from its snapshot, and store the run."""
        scenario, snapshot = self.scenario(name)
        plan = solve(apply(load_request(self.snapshot(snapshot)), scenario))
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT INTO run (scenario, snapshot, status, npv, risk, starts) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                            (name, snapshot, plan.status, plan.npv, plan.risk, canonical(plan.starts)))
        return plan

    def runs(self, name: str) -> list[Plan]:
        found = self.db.execute("SELECT status, npv, risk, starts FROM run WHERE scenario = ? ORDER BY id", (name,))
        return [Plan(status=s, starts=json.loads(starts), objective=npv, npv=npv, risk=risk)
                for s, npv, risk, starts in found]

"""Run: plan the demo export, print the planners' report, why P003 was deferred, the trade
between NPV and risk, what $1,000k more in 2028 and 2029 would change, and whether three runs
of the planner agree.

data/demo.json is GridCap tiny, a fictional utility's portfolio. Its path is taken from this
file's folder, never from the working directory, so the report is the same wherever Run starts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from cipt.__main__ import main
from cipt.data import read_request
from cipt.goals import frontier
from cipt.scenario import Scenario, apply, diff
from cipt.solve import solve
from cipt.trust import harness

DEMO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "demo.json"


def show_frontier() -> None:
    """One line per plan on the frontier, from the best NPV to the most risk removed."""
    print()
    print("NPV against risk removed:")
    for point in frontier(read_request(DEMO)):
        print(f"  NPV ${point.npv:,.0f}k  risk removed ${point.risk:,.1f}k  funds {', '.join(point.plan.funded)}")


def show_scenario() -> None:
    """The base plan against a scenario that adds $1,000k to the budgets of 2028 and 2029."""
    request = read_request(DEMO)
    more = Scenario("more money", budget={y: request.budget[y] + 1_000 for y in (2028, 2029)},
                    note="the rate case allows more capital")
    base, other = solve(request), solve(apply(request, more))
    d = diff(base, other)
    print()
    print(f"scenario {more.name}: NPV ${base.npv:,.0f}k -> ${other.npv:,.0f}k")
    print(f"  selected {', '.join(d.selected) or 'none'}; deferred {', '.join(d.deferred) or 'none'}")
    for pid, before, after in d.shifted:
        print(f"  shifted {pid} {before} -> {after}")


def show_trust() -> None:
    """Plan the export three times from scratch and say whether the plans agree."""
    runs = harness(json.loads(DEMO.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), runs=3)
    print()
    print(f"{len(runs.digests)} runs, same plan: {runs.same}, plan digest {runs.digests[0][:12]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    status = main([str(DEMO), "--why", "P003"])
    show_frontier()
    show_scenario()
    show_trust()
    raise SystemExit(status)

"""Snapshots, scenarios and runs in one SQLite file (lesson 12.1.4).

A snapshot is the export exactly as received, stored as canonical JSON under the sha256 of that
JSON, so a run can always be traced to the bytes it planned from, and a changed byte is caught when
the snapshot is read. A run stores the scenario, the snapshot's hash and the plan it produced.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

from .data import load_request
from .plan import Plan
from .scenario import Scenario, apply
from .solve import solve

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshot (hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scenario (name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, snapshot TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES snapshot(hash),
                                     body TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, scenario TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES scenario(name),
                                snapshot TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, npv REAL, risk REAL,
                                starts TEXT NOT NULL);
"""


def canonical(raw: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(raw, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def content_hash(raw: dict) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(raw).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class Store:
    def __init__(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(path)
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)

    def save_snapshot(self, raw: dict) -> str:
        digest = content_hash(raw)
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO snapshot VALUES (?, ?)", (digest, canonical(raw)))
        return digest

    def snapshot(self, digest: str) -> dict:
        (body,) = self.db.execute("SELECT body FROM snapshot WHERE hash = ?", (digest,)).fetchone()
        raw = json.loads(body)
        if content_hash(raw) != digest:
            raise ValueError(f"snapshot {digest[:12]} does not match its hash")
        return raw

    def save_scenario(self, scenario: Scenario, snapshot: str) -> None:
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO scenario VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                            (scenario.name, snapshot, canonical(scenario.to_dict())))

    def scenario(self, name: str) -> tuple[Scenario, str]:
        body, snapshot = self.db.execute("SELECT body, snapshot FROM scenario WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchone()
        return Scenario.from_dict(json.loads(body)), snapshot

    def run(self, name: str) -> Plan:
        """Plan a stored scenario from its snapshot, and store the run."""
        scenario, snapshot = self.scenario(name)
        plan = solve(apply(load_request(self.snapshot(snapshot)), scenario))
        with self.db:
            self.db.execute("INSERT INTO run (scenario, snapshot, status, npv, risk, starts) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                            (name, snapshot, plan.status, plan.npv, plan.risk, canonical(plan.starts)))
        return plan

    def runs(self, name: str) -> list[Plan]:
        found = self.db.execute("SELECT status, npv, risk, starts FROM run WHERE scenario = ? ORDER BY id", (name,))
        return [Plan(status=s, starts=json.loads(starts), objective=npv, npv=npv, risk=risk)
                for s, npv, risk, starts in found]

"""Run: plan the demo export, print the planners' report, why P003 was deferred, the trade
between NPV and risk, and what $1,000k more in 2028 and 2029 would change.

data/demo.json is GridCap tiny, a fictional utility's portfolio. Its path is taken from this
file's folder, never from the working directory, so the report is the same wherever Run starts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from cipt.__main__ import main
from cipt.data import read_request
from cipt.goals import frontier
from cipt.scenario import Scenario, apply, diff
from cipt.solve import solve

DEMO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "demo.json"


def show_frontier() -> None:
    """One line per plan on the frontier, from the best NPV to the most risk removed."""
    print()
    print("NPV against risk removed:")
    for point in frontier(read_request(DEMO)):
        print(f"  NPV ${point.npv:,.0f}k  risk removed ${point.risk:,.1f}k  funds {', '.join(point.plan.funded)}")


def show_scenario() -> None:
    """The base plan against a scenario that adds $1,000k to the budgets of 2028 and 2029."""
    request = read_request(DEMO)
    more = Scenario("more money", budget={y: request.budget[y] + 1_000 for y in (2028, 2029)},
                    note="the rate case allows more capital")
    base, other = solve(request), solve(apply(request, more))
    d = diff(base, other)
    print()
    print(f"scenario {more.name}: NPV ${base.npv:,.0f}k -> ${other.npv:,.0f}k")
    print(f"  selected {', '.join(d.selected) or 'none'}; deferred {', '.join(d.deferred) or 'none'}")
    for pid, before, after in d.shifted:
        print(f"  shifted {pid} {before} -> {after}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    status = main([str(DEMO), "--why", "P003"])
    show_frontier()
    show_scenario()
    raise SystemExit(status)
